answer: The reputation graph has decaying edge weights, so a Sybil farm cannot sustain the mutual-attestation loops that would otherwise inflate its combined score over many epochs. This holds because a newly minted alias starts worthless, so the attacker must first farm credibility on each one before it can swing a verdict. What this achieves is a system where the cost of an attack is public and provable, so the whole network can trust verdicts without trusting any single identity.
